Fix CLAUDE.md. Change no source code. Do not commit.

Its Build Commands section is an unfilled template, which means both Claude Code and Codex are guessing. Fill it in with the real, verified commands: the three schemes (ScreenTime, ScreenTime-UIOnly, DeviceActivityReportExtension) built SEQUENTIALLY with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, because concurrent builds hit "build database is locked", and the test command against the iOS-26 iPhone 17 simulator by id, not name.

Also make sure it states plainly: never commit, never create or switch branches, the four invariants, the single ManagedSettings enforcement writer, never call stopMonitoring() with no arguments, and the test conventions (pure XCTest, Foundation-only, no @testable import, ScreenTimeTests is filesystem-synchronized, production Shared files need hand-added per-target membership).

Note that AGENTS.md is now a symlink to this file, so Codex reads it too. Write it so it makes sense to any coding agent, not just you. Do not mention Claude-specific tooling in it.

Show me the diff before writing.

Three fixes before you write it.

1. Do NOT strip the skill names. Claude Code invokes /review-loop and /ultrareview-local by name; removing them breaks it. Keep the names AND add a fallback so any agent works. Phrase it like: "Invoke the /review-loop skill. If you have no skill loader, read .claude/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md, .claude/agents/health-reviewer.md, and .claude/agents/bug-confirmer.md, and follow that pipeline exactly." Same for /ultrareview-local.

2. Show me all three build commands in full. The diff only renders one legible xcodebuild line (ScreenTime). Confirm ScreenTime-UIOnly and DeviceActivityReportExtension are written out completely, each on its own line, in order.

3. You introduced two contradictions with the skill file. CLAUDE.md now says build verify is sequential, but review-loop/SKILL.md Phase 4 says to run all build commands in PARALLEL. And CLAUDE.md still says "Multi-agent parallel health check (one reviewer per scope)," while the skill says to review each scope INLINE, sequentially, and explicitly NOT to use the Task tool. Fix BOTH files so they agree: builds sequential, health check inline and sequential, no Task tool.

Then show me the full proposed CLAUDE.md and the diff to review-loop/SKILL.md. Change no source code. Do not commit.

Good, all three fixed. Two additions, then write it.

1. You dropped three sections without replacing them: "Project-specific Never rules", "iOS-specific limitations to work around", and "Pending and deferred (do not start without explicit user approval)". Restore them with real content:

Never rules: never run xcodegen (the project has extensions not in any spec, and it would wipe manual pbxproj membership); the DeviceActivityMonitor extension has a tight memory budget, so keep allocations minimal there; xcodebuild rewrites project.pbxproj build-file ordering as membership-neutral churn, so `git checkout HEAD -- ScreenTime.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` if it pollutes the diff.

iOS limitations: the DeviceActivity extension is out-of-process and communicates with the host only through the App Group and Darwin notifications; Screen Time framework code must be gated `#if !targetEnvironment(simulator)` or the UIOnly scheme and tests break; there is no API to read accumulated app usage, only threshold callbacks.

Pending and deferred, do not start without my explicit approval: the R1 through R5 structural persistence fixes; the L1 through L5 security findings (L1 is a beta free-Pro toggle that ships in Release and risks App Store rejection); the Family Controls distribution entitlement, which must be requested separately per bundle ID including each extension.

2. There is an untracked ScreenTime/Sources/Probe/ folder on disk, wired into nothing (a DEBUG-only DeviceActivity threshold probe). Add a line telling agents it exists, that it is intentionally unwired, and not to restore or delete it without asking.

Then write both files exactly as proposed plus these additions. Show me the final diff. Change no source code. Do not commit.

The Wave 2 gate failed on trivial compile errors, not a design problem: a missing `import os` and two wrong method calls (getInt/setInt) in SharedDataStore+Limits.swift. That is exactly the kind of thing you should fix yourself and keep going, not stop for.

Clarifying the rule for the rest of this run, and apply it going forward: the three-attempt limit means you get up to three fix-and-re-gate cycles per wave. A compile error, a missing import, a typo'd method name, a wrong signature, or any mechanical mistake in code YOU just wrote does not consume an attempt and does not trigger a stop. Just fix it and re-run the gate. Only STOP and surface to me when: a gate still fails after three genuine fix cycles, OR you would have to weaken an existing test / invariant / architecture decision to make it pass, OR you hit one of the three "must never happen" conditions. Mechanical errors in your own new code are never a reason to stop.

So: fix the import and the getInt/setInt calls now. Re-run the Wave 2 gate (three schemes sequentially + full suite + the A and C greps). If green, continue through Waves 3-6 under the clarified rule. Wave 3 still must not modify any existing planner test.

Two things to confirm while you fix: (1) the full suite was 848 tests in an earlier run and you report 789 now. Tell me why the count dropped. (2) You said the Probe folder is tracked at HEAD, not untracked as the spec assumed. Confirm you have not modified or wired it, and that the discrepancy changes nothing in your plan.

Report each wave's build result, gate status, and the A/C greps as you go. Stop only under the three conditions above.
Since this app is in beta I want to be able to delete a limit once it is reached to test again, how do I do that?
check for any bugs if everything you have implemented. I want this ti work properly
when you find a bug, verify it is real, after verification, fix it
